_comment: Hand-authored. Bank 6 object handlers: chasing enemies $1D-$1F ($9D0A-$9DF9). The generators subtract these.

regions.name: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): first frame?
regions.description: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): type bit 7 set goes to the per-frame code (`$9D46`). Stats of the three types: collision flags `$50` (bit 6 = the Enemy Eraser does not take it, bit 4 = the big burst when it dies), drawing flags 3, art block `$12`, dies as type 8; hit points 1 / 3 / 6 (x 16 by `$C165`), attack 16 / 48 / 80. **No area scaling and no tier table: the strength is the same in every area** (RUN at areas 5 and 0: hit points 16 / 48 / 96, attack 16 / 48 / 80).

TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): hit points x 16
regions.description: `JSR $C165` (`$D385`): the table's hit points are widened into `$0740` : `$0590`.

TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): random place, free cell?
regions.description: `JSR $C0F3` (random x 32-223, y 40-183) and `JSR $9A53` (the class under it, `$8425`).

TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): blocked: try again
regions.description: `JMP $9B17`: removed, the type put back, a new place next frame. (Unlike types `$0E` / `$0F` the preset `$0728` is not tested: a spawner's position is overwritten.)

regions.name: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): introduction
TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): set-up
TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): first timer
regions.description: `$07A0` := `$1E`: 30 frames from the end of the introduction to the first decision.

regions.name: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): direction
regions.description: `$0668` := 4 (down). The velocity is zero until the first decision, so it stands still for 90 frames. RUN: each type spawned alone in the labyrinth state at area 5 with `$0728` preset, the player held at (60, 60), 600 frames.

TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): the decision timer
regions.description: `$07A0` is decremented; non-zero skips to the picture.

regions.name: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): type `$1D` does not shoot
regions.description: A type under `$1E` skips the shot. Type `$73` enters at `$9D5F`, after this test, so it never fires.

regions.name: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): a free slot
TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): the shot
regions.description: `LDA #$0B / JSR $C105` (`$FA4B`): a type-`$0B` enemy shot aimed at the player, made at this object. RUN: types `$1E` and `$1F` fired 10 and 11 shots in 600 frames, `$1D` none.

regions.name: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): the next timer
TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): type `$1F` is twice as quick
TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): the direction to the player, rounded
regions.description: `JSR $C0FF` (0-15), +2 and AND `$0C`: the nearest of the four straight directions (0 right, 4 down, 8 left, 12 up), kept in `$15`.

regions.name: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): heading away?
regions.description: The opposite of that direction ((`$15` + 8) AND `$0C`) compared with the current `$0668`: if they differ, take `$15`.

regions.name: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): heading away: sideways instead
regions.description: Equal (the carry is set): `$15` := (`$15` + `$15` + 1) / 2 AND `$0C`, which is a direction at right angles to it (0 -> 4, 4 -> 8, 8 -> 4, 12 -> 8). So an enemy moving straight away from the player turns aside first and toward it at the next decision.

regions.name: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): new direction
TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): velocity
regions.description: `JSR $C102` (`$F8CE`): speed from the direction and the speed class. RUN: the direction changed at frames 89 (end of the introduction + timer), then every 20-60 frames.

regions.name: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): the type `$73` branch
regions.description: Type `$F3` (type `$73` with its bit 7) takes a different picture. **CORRECTION: this branch is LIVE. Type `$73` has its own handler at `$B96E` that jumps into the middle of this one (`JMP $9D26`, `JMP $9D5F`, `JMP $9D95`), so type `$73` runs it every frame. The earlier text said 'no dispatch entry sends type `$73` here, so it cannot be taken' - true of the dispatch table, wrong about the code.**

regions.name: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): that branch: flip mask
TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): that branch: flip
regions.description: `JSR $9B09`: flips bit 6 of the palette when (`$41` AND A) = 0, i.e. every 4th frame. **Called by type `$73` every frame** (see `$9D95`), contradicting the earlier 'never made'.

regions.name: TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): that branch: on
TYPES $1D / $1E / $1F (A GROUND ENEMY THAT STEPS TOWARD THE PLAYER): picture phase
regions.description: `JSR $C0A5` with step `$20` over 2 phases (a change every 8 frames).
